description: Encoded clips with a LUT no longer fall to the CPU oracle: the YUV door of the develop session carries the LUT path and binding (strength, managed interpretation). To make the shared LUT stage match the CPU lattice, the 3D table is now RGBA32F read with texelFetch and blended by hand (it was RGBA16F through the hardware filter, which differed from the CPU by 1 LSB on 3-5% of samples). Device parity of an encoded frame with a 17^3 LUT against the CPU oracle: 0 LSB, 0.0000% mismatch on an 8-bit and a Mi-Log P010 case (bound 0.01%, unchanged); the other four encoded parity tests still pass. The shader validator's pin on the old texel-centre mapping becomes a pin on the eight-corner lattice read.
